segments.text: A hundred metres under the North Sea, a diver's lifeline snaps. He has about five minutes of gas.
No chance. Five minutes of gas doesn't last half an hour. Let's go look.
September {2012|twenty twelve}. Chris Lemons is working on an oil well. His breathing gas comes down a cable from the ship.
The ship's positioning system fails. It drifts. His cable snags, pulls tight, and snaps.
In the dark, he climbs on top of the structure and waits. Then his gas runs out.
Up top, they watch him on a robot's camera. His movements slow. Then stop.
Around thirty minutes later, the ship is back. Diver Dave Yuasa hauls him to the bell, sure he's carrying a body.
Helmet off. A crewmate breathes into his mouth. And Chris Lemons breathes again.
Best guess: the cold, and oxygen-rich gas. No lasting damage. I was wrong. Case closed.
